results.summary: This Wokwi design displays a mirrored '3' (or 'M') on a 7-segment display when inputs IN0, IN2, IN4, and IN6 are set high. An LED also lights to indicate the correct combination. It uses a shared Tiny Tapeout tile with 8 inputs and 8 outputs, but only the specified inputs matter for the intended behaviour. The design is a simple introductory project, likely created for educational purposes.

This Wokwi project checks a 3-bit input against the code 267 (binary 011 for 2, 110 for 6, 111 for 7 on DIP switches) and displays the number 4 on a 7-segment display when matched. The inputs are provided via IN0, IN1, and IN2 (and possibly more), and the output drives a 7-segment display. The design is a simple combinational lock demonstration with no external hardware beyond the display. It has minimal documentation, but the intended function is clear.

This Wokwi design combines AND, NOT, and flip-flop logic gates to connect inputs IN0-IN3 to outputs OUT0-OUT2. The exact function is not precisely described beyond 'AND and NOT and FlipFlop logic gates', and the test method is simply observing LEDs. The project uses four inputs and three outputs; no external hardware other than LED indicators is mentioned. The documentation is very thin, making detailed assessment difficult.

This Wokwi design continually outputs the letter 'A' on a 7-segment display unless any input is active, in which case the display changes. It uses a clock at 10000 Hz and a logic circuit to drive the display. The test involves running the clock and observing the output while toggling inputs. No external hardware beyond the display and input switches is required.

This Wokwi project implements a standard 4-bit adder using AND, XOR, and OR gates, with a 5-bit output to handle overflow. The inputs are arranged as element-wise pairs: IN0 and IN1 are the LSBs of the two numbers, IN2 and IN3 are the next bits, and so on. The design can be tested by performing 4-bit additions on paper and comparing with the circuit's outputs. No external hardware is required beyond the inputs and outputs.

This Wokwi design sets all outputs high when inputs IN0, IN1, IN2, and IN3 are high; otherwise, the outputs are low. The description claims that 'power goes in, power maybe comes out?' and that no testing is needed. The project is extremely simple and lacks detailed documentation. It uses 8 inputs and 8 outputs, but the logic only involves four inputs.

This Wokwi design connects inputs to outputs through a couple of logic gates, with no specific function described. The documentation states that there is nothing to test and no external hardware is used. It appears to be a trivial passthrough or simple gate arrangement with minimal documentation. The design likely serves as a basic exercise in using the Wokwi editor.

This Wokwi project implements a 4-bit adder that outputs a 5-bit sum. Two 4-bit numbers are input via IN0-IN3 and IN4-IN6 (with IN7 possibly unused), and the result is presented on OUT0-OUT4. Testing involves setting input switches to form two numbers and verifying the binary sum on the outputs. No external hardware is required beyond LEDs or other indicators.

This Wokwi project is completely non-functional; the documentation states that it does not work and cannot be tested. All pins are labeled N/A, and no external hardware is used. It appears to be an empty or unfinished design, possibly a placeholder or failed experiment. There is no discernible function or purpose.

This Wokwi design implements a NAND gate with a NOT gate on one input, using inputs IN2 and IN3 and output OUT3. The documented truth table specifies that output is high except when both inputs are high (for the NAND function after inversion). Testing can be done with LEDs or other indicators. The design is a simple logic gate demonstration with clear documentation.
